title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: gridmicrotex renders LaTeX math equations native R grid graphics objects (grobs). uses MicroTeX C++ library layout engine — MicroTeX parses LaTeX, builds TeX box model, computes exact glyph coordinates. package intercepts layout data maps native grid primitives (pathGrob, segmentsGrob, rectGrob, textGrob), producing gTree works R graphics device resolution. Key features: external LaTeX installation required — MicroTeX fully embedded Resolution-independent vector output R devices (PNG, PDF, SVG, …) Full math support: fractions, roots, integrals, matrices, Greek letters, accents, delimiters, Two bundled math fonts: Lete Sans Math (sans-serif, default) STIX Two Math (serif); additional fonts via load_font() Color support via \textcolor{} ggplot2 integration geom_latex() element_latex() CJK multilingual text \text{} blocks

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: \mark{name} macro records named anchor position inside formula. grobMark() resolves anchor pair grid units, ready drive arrow, callout, grob. mark works nesting level — top-level tokens, compound sub-expression like b^2, even inside superscript fraction. position inherits surrounding transform (font shrink scripts, scaling, rotation), anchor lands rendered glyph rather pre-layout offset.  returned units carry grob’s viewport position hjust/vjust, can pass straight grid.points, grid.segments, grid drawing function — manual offset arithmetic. \mark records single point, span. centre callout multi-glyph term, place mark term’s end shift drawing code, place pair marks (\mark{l}…\mark{r}) use midpoint.
code: g <- latex_grob(   r"($a^2 + b\mark{term}^2 \mark{equals}= c^2$)",   x = 0.5, y = 0.4,   gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 28) ) grid::grid.newpage() grid::grid.draw(g)  # Callout 1: the "=" sign, pointed at from above. mk_eq <- grobMark(g, "equals") grid::grid.segments(mk_eq$x, mk_eq$y + unit(15, "mm"),                     mk_eq$x, mk_eq$y + unit(3, "mm"),                     arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),                     gp = grid::gpar(col = "red")) grid::grid.text("equals", x = mk_eq$x, y = mk_eq$y + unit(18, "mm"),                 gp = grid::gpar(col = "red", fontsize = 11))  # Callout 2: the b^2 term, pointed at from below — the mark sits at the # end of the term, including the superscript's smaller scale. mk_bsq <- grobMark(g, "term") grid::grid.segments(mk_bsq$x - unit(6, "mm"), mk_bsq$y - unit(15, "mm"),                     mk_bsq$x - unit(2, "mm"), mk_bsq$y - unit(3, "mm"),                     arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),                     gp = grid::gpar(col = "blue")) grid::grid.text("b² term",                 x = mk_bsq$x - unit(7, "mm"),                 y = mk_bsq$y - unit(18, "mm"),                 just = "right",                 gp = grid::gpar(col = "blue", fontsize = 11))

title: Introduction to gridmicrotex
text: gridmicrotex supports two rendering modes math glyphs: "typeface" (default): Renders glyphs native text using math font’s typeface. produces selectable, searchable, accessible text PDF SVG output. Bundled math fonts (Lete Sans Math, STIX Two Math) registered via load_font() read directly OTF files — system-wide font install required. Requires device supports R 4.3 glyph engine (e.g., ragg::agg_png(), svglite::svglite(), grDevices::cairo_pdf()). devices (e.g., base pdf() device), package automatically falls back path mode warning. "path": Renders glyph filled vector path. works R graphics devices produces pixel-perfect output. However, text PDF/SVG output selectable searchable. Important: use showtext::showtext_auto() typeface mode. showtext package globally intercepts text rendering converts vector paths. silently defeats typeface mode, causing math glyphs appear paths instead native text — even devices like svglite ragg fully support font embedding. need showtext parts plot, disable drawing LaTeX formulas:
code: # Default typeface mode (selectable text in PDF/SVG) grid.latex("E = mc^2", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 24))  # Explicit path mode (works everywhere, but text is not selectable) grid.latex("E = mc^2", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 24), render_mode = "path") showtext::showtext_auto(FALSE) grid.latex("E = mc^2", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 24))  # typeface mode works correctly

text: define_macro() registers zero-argument shorthands expanded text substitution expression reaches MicroTeX. Handy recurring notation:  Macro names must ASCII letters. Expansion iterates fixed point, macros can reference macros. Use list_macros() see currently registered ones, clear_macros() (arguments) drop . parameterised macros (0–9 arguments) scoped single expression, MicroTeX also accepts plain-TeX \def:  \def definitions live duration expression appear , right tool parameterised abbreviation local one label. title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
text: geom_latex() works like geom_text() interprets label aesthetic LaTeX math string. can also map size (font size points) colour aesthetics usual. element_latex() replaces text theme element label rendered LaTeX math.  Dollar-sign delimiters ($...$) stripped automatically, "\\frac{}{b}" "$\\frac{}{b}$" produce output.
code: df <- data.frame(   x = 1:3,   y = 1:3,   eq = c("$x^2$", "\\frac{a}{b}", "$\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$"),   col = c("red", "blue", "green") )  ggplot(df, aes(x, y,                 label = eq,                 colour = col,                 size = c(14, 18, 14))) +   geom_latex() +   scale_colour_identity() +   scale_size_identity() +   labs(     x = "$\\beta_1 \\cdot x + \\beta_0$",     y = "$\\mathrm{mpg}$"   ) +   theme(     axis.title.x = element_latex(fontsize = 14),     axis.title.y = element_latex(fontsize = 14)   )

title: Using LaTeX Math in ggplot2
